description_full: Karooooo Ltd. provides software applications for fleet management, mobile asset tracking, workforce management, and video solutions in South Africa, the rest of Africa, Europe, the Asia-Pacific, the Middle East, and the United States. It operates through Cartrack, Carzuka, and Karooooo Logistics segments. The company offers Cartrack, a mobility SaaS cloud that provides systems integration, fleet management and administration, field worker management, video-based safety, risk mitigation and compliance, delivery management, and reporting solutions; and Karooooo Logistics, a software application for management of last-mile delivery and general operational logistics. It also provides physical and e-commerce vehicle buying and selling marketplace. The company serves consumers and sole proprietors, small and medium-sized businesses, and large enterprises. Karooooo Ltd. was founded in 2001 and is headquartered in Singapore.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 7K people. Revenue per employee of $37K ranks in the bottom quartile among Technology peers, improving at 16%/yr — growing workforce leverage. Each employee generates $7K of free cash flow annually.
financial_summary: Karooooo Ltd. is a small-cap technology business with a $1.9B market cap on $270M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +11% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 36% against a 10% cost of capital — a 26-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 66% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $54M in free cash flow — roughly 20 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.06× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -21.3% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 26× is fortress-like.
Shareholder yield is only 1.9%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 68% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 43% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 8% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 37% and a beta of 1.05, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.48 vs 5y 1.07), so read it loosely.

val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $53.18 (margin of safety -18%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 24%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $33.78 to $87.42 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
Multiples send mixed signals against Technology peers: cheaper on EV/EBITDA 1.2 vs 16.4, richer on P/FCF 36.1 vs 25.4 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 31% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 2.8% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 2.8% (vs the 8% bar).
The 5 covering analysts target $74.48 on average, 18% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 36% clears the cost of capital of 10.0% by 26pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.32).
It runs a 66% gross margin and converts 20% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality is mixed: cash conversion of 2.06x, but high accruals (-21.3% of assets).
ROE of 32% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.6x equity multiplier).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $55.1M.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 14.2, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 10.5% over 3 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 9% of profits supports about 3.3% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Analysts expect 18.6% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own 67.6%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 18%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (21 sales, net $18.4M sold).
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.9% (2.4% in dividends).
people: With about 7,395 employees, each generates about $37K of revenue, 0.1x the Technology median, and productivity has risen 15.7% a year.
That works out to $7K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
